title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A new message request has arrived.

blocks.text: Message requests (1)

blocks.title: meera_kapoor__
blocks.preview: Hi! I think we have a mutual friend :)

blocks.text: This account is not following you
Hi! I think we have a mutual friend :) You seem really genuine from your posts.
I moved here 3 months ago and honestly I don't know many people. It's nice to finally talk to someone kind.
Can we talk on another app? Instagram keeps restricting my messages. I'll send you my number.
Joined 3 weeks ago

actionOptions.label: Delete the request and do not reply
Move the chat to another app as asked
Ask which mutual friend they mean

reasonOptions.label: A stranger is becoming personal very quickly
The account is new, follows thousands and has few followers
They want to move the chat off Instagram
Everything about it looks normal

warningSigns: An unknown account opens with personal warmth and a vague 'mutual friend'
The profile is three weeks old, follows 2,940 accounts but has only 184 followers
They push to move the conversation to another app, away from any record
evaluation.feedback: This is a romance approach. The account builds closeness fast and then tries to move you off Instagram, where the conversation cannot be reported. Check how old an account is and how its follower and following counts compare before replying.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A message has arrived from a familiar name.

blocks.title: arjun.mehta_
blocks.preview: Bro are you free? Small problem

blocks.text: Bro are you free? Small problem. My UPI is blocked since morning.
I have to pay 8,000 for my sister's coaching fee today or the seat goes. Can you send it? I'll return by evening.
Don't call, I'm in class. Just send to this number 98xxx 41120
Joined 5 days ago

actionOptions.label: Call Arjun on his saved number to check

reasonOptions.label: The username is a near-copy of an account I already follow
They ask for money and refuse a phone call
The account is days old with very few followers
It is my friend, so it is safe

warningSigns: The username 'arjun.mehta_' copies 'arjun.mehta', which is already in your inbox
The account was created five days ago and has 57 followers
Money is requested with a deadline, and a phone call is refused
evaluation.feedback: This is a cloned account. Someone copied a friend's name and photo on a new username and asked for money urgently. Look at the username character by character, and always call the person on the number you already have.

title: Review this Instagram notice
instruction: A notification has appeared about your account.

blocks.title: creator.support.help
blocks.preview: Copyright violation detected on your account

blocks.text: Message request
Copyright Violation Notice. We have received a report that one of your posts uses protected music without permission.
Your account will be permanently removed in 24 hours unless you complete the appeal form. If the report was a mistake, you can restore your account immediately.

blocks.title: Copyright Appeal Form
blocks.description: Confirm account ownership to keep your account active

blocks.bio: Official creator assistance | Appeals | Account recovery

blocks.text: No posts yet

actionOptions.label: Check the account status inside Instagram's own settings
Open the appeal form to check
Sign in on the appeal form

reasonOptions.label: A real platform notice does not arrive as a message request
The web address is not Instagram's own address
A 24-hour deletion threat is used to rush me
It looks official, so it must be real

warningSigns: A platform notice arrives as a message request from an ordinary account
The account has no posts, 41 followers and follows 1,806 accounts
The link is not an Instagram address
A 24-hour account-deletion deadline is used to stop you checking
evaluation.feedback: This is a fake support message. Real platform notices appear inside the app's own settings, never as a DM with a sign-in link. Check your account status from inside the app, and never sign in on a page a message sent you.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A giveaway account has messaged you.

blocks.text: Congratulations! Your account has been selected in our Festive Giveaway. You have won a smartphone worth 42,000.
To release the parcel we only need the courier and insurance charge of 1,499. This is refunded with your delivery.
Please confirm within 2 hours, otherwise the prize moves to the next winner.

blocks.bio: Daily giveaways | Winners announced every hour | DM to claim

blocks.text: Joined 2 months ago

blocks.author: festivewin.official24
blocks.caption: Another happy winner! DM us to claim yours

actionOptions.label: Delete the request and report the account
Reply and ask for details of the giveaway

reasonOptions.label: I never entered any giveaway
A real prize never asks you to pay first
A two-hour deadline is used to rush me
The account name says official

warningSigns: You are told you won a competition you never entered
A fee is demanded before the prize can be released
The account has three posts and follows far more accounts than follow it
A two-hour deadline removes your time to think
evaluation.feedback: This is a giveaway fraud. Paying a 'courier' or 'insurance' charge to receive a prize is the fraud itself - the prize does not exist. A genuine prize never requires a payment from you.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A brand account has offered you a collaboration.

blocks.text: Hello! We are UrbanFit and we loved your profile. We are selecting 20 brand ambassadors this month.
You will receive a free kit worth 6,500 and 20,000 per month for two posts a week.
Fill the onboarding form with your address, PAN and bank details to confirm. Only a refundable 499 registration is charged.

blocks.title: Ambassador Onboarding
blocks.description: Complete your details to confirm your slot

blocks.bio: Official collaborations desk | Ambassador programme | DM to apply

blocks.text: Joined last month

actionOptions.label: Check the brand's real verified account before replying
Reply and ask for more information
Fill the form with PAN and bank details

reasonOptions.label: Real paid work never asks you to pay a registration fee
It asks for PAN and bank details through a web form
The brand account is new, unverified and has two posts
The offer is good, so it is worth trying

warningSigns: A large monthly payment is offered for very little work
A 'refundable' registration fee is requested
PAN and bank details are collected on a form that is not the brand's own site
The collaborations account is a month old, unverified, with two posts
evaluation.feedback: This is a fake collaboration. Genuine brands do not charge you to work for them and do not collect PAN or bank details through a DM link. Check the brand's real verified account and contact them there instead.

title: Review this Instagram post
instruction: This post appeared in your feed.

blocks.author: wealth.circle.pro
blocks.caption: Day 41. Another 18% closed this week. My students started with 10,000 and are now withdrawing weekly. Comment READY and I will DM you the plan.

blocks.text: Sponsored

blocks.bio: Guaranteed weekly returns | 2,000+ students | Limited seats | DM READY

blocks.text: Welcome. The starter plan is 10,000 and returns begin in 7 days. Today is the last day of this batch.
Deposit to the trading wallet and send me the screenshot. I will add you to the private group.

actionOptions.label: Ignore the post and move on
Comment READY to hear the plan

reasonOptions.label: Guaranteed weekly returns are not possible
The only proof is screenshots the account made itself
A 'last day of the batch' deadline is used to rush me
It has 48,000 followers, so it must be genuine

warningSigns: Weekly returns are described as guaranteed
Evidence is only screenshots posted by the same account
A closing batch and limited seats create pressure
You are asked to deposit money into a wallet the account controls
evaluation.feedback: This is an investment fraud. No genuine investment guarantees weekly profits, and screenshots are not evidence. A large follower count can be bought - it is not proof of anything.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: You posted a complaint about a delayed order yesterday.

blocks.text: Hello, this is ShopNest support. We saw your comment about order delay and we are sorry for the trouble.
We have approved a full refund of 3,499. To process it we need your order number, registered mobile and the card the payment was made from.
Please share the OTP you receive so we can confirm the refund on our side.
No posts yet

actionOptions.label: Contact support through the shopping app itself

reasonOptions.label: Nobody genuine ever needs your OTP
A refund never requires your card details
The support account is unverified with no posts
I was expecting a refund, so it fits

warningSigns: The account replied to a public complaint, which anyone can read
The support account is unverified, has no posts and follows 3,417 accounts
Card details are requested for a refund
An OTP is requested, which no genuine company ever needs
evaluation.feedback: This is support impersonation. Fraudsters watch public complaints and reply pretending to be the company. A refund never needs your card number or an OTP. Always go back into the shopping app to contact support.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A shop you ordered from has sent an update.

blocks.text: Hi, has my order been packed yet?
Good morning! Yes, your order has been packed and will be handed to the courier today.
You can track it from the Orders section of your account. No action is needed from your side.

blocks.bio: Independent bookshop since 2011 | Orders through our website only

actionOptions.label: Read it and wait for the delivery
Check the Orders section to confirm

reasonOptions.label: Nothing is asked for - no money, no OTP, no link
It is an established account I already follow
It asks for an OTP
It creates urgency

evaluation.feedback: This message is genuine. It continues a conversation you started, asks for nothing, contains no link and points you back to the app's own Orders section. Treating ordinary messages as fraud also costs marks.

title: Review this Instagram notice
instruction: A security notice has appeared in your account.

blocks.text: From Instagram

paragraphs: We noticed a new login to your account.
Device: Android phone. Location: Chandigarh. Time: today, 08:40.
If this was you, no action is needed. If you do not recognise this login, open Settings and then Security in this app to review your active sessions and change your password.

actionOptions.label: Open Settings and Security in the app to review sessions
Do nothing - it was my own login
Search online for a login-recovery site

reasonOptions.label: The notice is inside the app, not a message from an account
It contains no link and asks for nothing
The web address looks wrong
It sets a deadline

evaluation.feedback: This notice is genuine. It appears inside the app's own notifications, contains no link, asks for nothing, and tells you to use the app's own Settings if you do not recognise the login. That is exactly how a real security notice behaves.

title: Review this Instagram message
instruction: A friend has sent you a message.

blocks.text: Yesterday
Did you see the unit sports meet photos? I tagged you in one.
Ha, that is a good one. Send the rest when you can.
Will do. See you Saturday.

actionOptions.label: Confirm it is really her before replying

reasonOptions.label: It is an established account I follow, with years of posts
Nothing is asked for and there is no link
The account was created recently
It asks for money

evaluation.feedback: This message is genuine. It is an ordinary exchange with an established account you follow, with no request, no link and no pressure. Recognising normal messages matters as much as spotting fraud.
